design.summary: Add ONE small separate module, backend/services/detailing_responder.py plus detailing_config.json, beside demo_responder.py and sales_agent.py (same pattern as sales_agent: it borrows demo_responder's low-level helpers). A new hook in api/inbound.py runs after the normal storing and STOP handling and BEFORE the demo and AI hooks. It CLAIMS a lead message only if it belongs to a detailing template: the tapped message's context id resolves to a template_sent record whose template name is a detailing template, or (no usable context id) the sender's number is the recipient decoded from the wamid of a recent detailing send. A claimed message never reaches demo_responder or sales_agent, whatever demo_mode or sales_agent_mode say; every other message returns False after read-only lookups, so campaign 1 is byte-for-byte unchanged. For a claimed message: STOP words suppress always (+ one confirmation); a tap on the yes label or a typed plain yes (haan/ji/ok/demo) creates a hand-off and, only when the owner has switched the new flag detailing_mode on from his own WhatsApp, sends ONE fixed Hindi reply per template send (no AI, says it is automatic, no time/price/free promised); not-now is only logged; everything else (price, questions, 'send me the demo', voice notes) becomes a hand-off with no automatic text. No schema change, no .env change, no change to wa.py or the templates. A working prototype exists (NOT in the repo): C:\Users\ADMINI~1\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-Administrator-Desktop-wire-soldering\dec5451d-390d-44dc-a02c-fbc50c6d4a7c\scratchpad\proto\ (module 583 lines incl. comments, 92 tests, 27 of 27 mutants caught, whole suite 507 green on a patched scratch copy of the current backend, plus 10 unchanged agent-tool e2e tests).
trigger_rules: CLAIM by context: msg.context.id equals the wamid of a template_sent record (agent_activity, last 60 days) whose payload.template is listed in detailing_config.json OR contains the word 'detailing'. If the context id points to any OTHER template (campaign 1) the message is NOT claimed. Recognition is read-only (no write before a message is claimed).

CLAIM by number: no usable context id (typed text, a reply-swipe on our own auto-reply, or a BSP that drops it) AND the sender's number equals the 91xxxxxxxxxx decoded from the wamid of a detailing template_sent in the last 60 days AND no real-estate demo session is already open for that number. A last-4-digits match is deliberately NOT used (a collision could swallow a campaign-1 lead's 'send the demo').

YES = a tap whose NFC-normalised label is in the template's yes_labels, OR (typed_yes on) a whole message of at most 4 words made only of configured yes words (haan, ha, haa, ji, yes, ok, okay, demo, send, bhejo, dikhao, Devanagari and Gujarati forms such as हाँ, हां, जी, હા, જી) with no '?' and no digit.
NOT NOW = a tap on notnow_labels or a whole-message decline word (nahi, abhi nahi, no, later): event only; no reply, no hand-off, no suppression.

STOP = demo_responder._is_hard_stop (CRM list + Hindi, Gujarati, Hinglish: band karo, बंद करो, nahi chahiye, mat bhejo, no thanks, not interested) on the label, the typed text or a media caption: suppress ALWAYS, whatever the mode, and cancel the open hand-off.

OTHER = unknown label, any other text (price, questions, 'send me the demo for my studio please', 'ok thanks'), 'haan?' / 'demo?' with a question mark: hand-off at normal priority, no automatic text. MEDIA (voice note, image, document, location): hand-off, plus the optional media_reply once per 6 h.

The automatic reply goes out only if ALL hold: not paused (STOP ALL); detailing_mode on (or test and the number is in DEMO_TEST_NUMBERS); WhatsApp credentials present; number not suppressed; the lead's message is younger than 23 h; the template send is younger than 7 days; no wa.py reply was logged for this lead since the send; caps not reached; the per-send marker was acquired; the config is valid.

It never sends a first message: it only answers a message that just arrived, inside the 24 h window. The words 'send the demo' are never sent and a label containing them (or any STOP phrase) makes the config invalid.
flow_steps: 1. Webhook -> api/inbound.py stores the message exactly as today (agent_inbound_feed row; record_inbound suppresses a plain STOP). The new hook comes after this and before the demo and AI hooks.

2. detailing_responder.maybe_handle_lead_message(db, msg, sender, kind, body, trusted): untrusted request -> False. Read-only recognition (context id, else number). Not a detailing message -> return False with nothing written.
3. Claimed: the function returns True even if it later crashes (inbound.py returns, the demo and AI hooks are skipped); errors are logged and swallowed, the webhook still answers 200.
4. Write the marker 'det:<inbound wamid>' into demo_seen (PRIMARY KEY). Already there = a webhook retry -> stop.
5. Classify with the template's config entry: ignore (reaction, sticker, emoji, another business's auto-reply) | stop | yes | notnow | media | other.
6. Write one detailing_inbound agent_activity event (class, via, mode, template, masked phone).
7. stop -> demo_responder._suppress, cancel open hand-offs, send ONE confirmation (marker 'detstop:<phone>') only if automatic replies are allowed; end.
8. Suppressed number (not a STOP) -> event detailing_blocked, end. notnow -> end.

9. yes / other / media -> hand-off FIRST (agent_service.create_handoff, or append to the open hand-off of the last 24 h; priority high for yes), skipped for lead_ref 'Owner test' / 'Boss test' sends. The brief carries template name, send time, the lead's cleaned words (links and long digit runs removed) and the observation line.

10. Automatic reply (yes -> yes_reply, media -> media_reply) if every condition of the reply rule holds: acquire marker 'detsend:<template wamid>' (once per template send, tap and typed share it) or 'detmedia:<phone>:<6 h bucket>' BEFORE sending; send through demo_responder._send_text; write detailing_auto_reply or detailing_reply_failed; never retried.

11. Owner alert: a free-form WhatsApp to the owner only inside his own 24 h window (cap 20/day, none while paused) with lead name, what happened, 'Automatic reply: sent / not sent (reason)', 'reply by hand before HH:MM IST' and the wa.me link. Outside his window the hand-off card and the operator lane are the signal (no credit spent).
12. A person (closer draft + owner OK code, wa.py reply at autonomy stage 1) answers from the company number inside the 24 h window; the instant fixed reply only buys time.

13. Owner path (api/inbound.py owner branch -> detailing_responder.after_owner_message): DETAILING ON/OFF/TEST/STATUS set or report the flag; DETAILING RUN and the owner's own tap on a detailing test send show him the exact lead text plus 'Test run finished' in ANY mode, with no hand-off, no suppression, and his inbox row marked processed so the fast lane does not treat it as chat.

safety_rails: OFF by default: a missing agent_flags row means off. Only the owner's own verified WhatsApp message can write detailing_mode (whole-message regex, owner_channel chain: verified webhook + owner number); no API route can set it (api/agent.py exposes only GET /flags -> paused).
STOP ALL (paused flag) stops every automatic send and every owner alert; hand-off rows are still written.
Only a webhook request that passed the secret check is trusted; an untrusted request returns False and writes nothing.

Claim isolation: a claimed message is never passed to demo_responder or sales_agent, in any flag combination (probe_after.py: demo ON + agent ON + detailing OFF/ON, agent OFF + detailing ON). Non-detailing messages: False after read-only lookups.

Idempotent by construction: UNIQUE marker per inbound wamid (det:<wamid>), per template send (detsend:<template wamid>, shared by tap and typed yes), per STOP (detstop:<phone>) and per media window; markers are written BEFORE sending (at most once for the lead, at least once for the human signal because the hand-off is written first).
Suppression: checked before any answer; a STOP suppresses first, then gets one confirmation; a suppressed number is never answered or handed off again.

Caps: 1 automatic reply per template send, 2 per number per 24 h, 30 per day overall, 20 owner alerts per day, 1 media reply per 6 h; lead message must be younger than 23 h, template send younger than 7 days for an automatic reply (60 days for the claim).
No automatic reply once a person has replied (wa.py logs a reply_sent activity for the lead).
The lead's own words are never echoed back; the brand name is not echoed either; only validated config texts are ever sent.

Config validation at load (sales_agent.check_reply on every text, banned campaign words, AI/automatic + STOP present, labels <= 25 chars and not a demo trigger or stop phrase). A bad config = claim and hand-off only, nothing sent, DETAILING STATUS says CONFIG PROBLEM.
A test-send label ('Owner test' / 'Boss test') gets the reply but no hand-off or alert.
A provider failure never retries; the hand-off already exists and the alert says 'FAILED, reply by hand'.
Any exception is logged and swallowed; a recognised message stays claimed.
Python 3.9 compatible; no new table; no .env or config.py change.

Typed-yes false positives (an 'ok' that is not a yes): the text is harmless, and the module limits it (whole message, <= 4 words, no '?', one reply per template send, no reply after a person answered, 7-day template age). A studio that answers from a DIFFERENT number is an unknown sender again (today's behaviour) because only the original chat carries the context id and the wamid number.

alternatives_considered.option: A1. Extend demo_responder.py (add 'detailing' as another project type or flow)
alternatives_considered.verdict: REJECT, but reuse its helpers by import
alternatives_considered.why: demo_responder.py is an 866-line real-estate state machine (budget / BHK / visit slot) pinned by about 100 tests, and its mode flag demo_mode is shared with campaign 1 and, per agent/memory.md, already ON: a detailing reply hung on it would go live the moment the code is deployed, and DEMO OFF/TEST (the only brake) would also switch off campaign-1 demos. Its entry point returns early unless the phrase 'send the demo' or an open session exists (demo_responder.py:705-706), so a plain yes tap needs new branches in the most sensitive function of the live webhook, and the playbook (section 10) requires a full 3-lens re-review for anything that changes what a lead can receive. It also cannot stop the AI persona from answering detailing leads. The separate module borrows its send/suppress/mask/hand-off helpers exactly as sales_agent.py already does (sales_agent.py:60, 173, 349, 356, 590, 802).

alternatives_considered.option: A2. New small module detailing_responder.py + config + 3 hook lines + one owner command (this design)
alternatives_considered.why: Smallest change that meets every constraint: claim isolation makes the real-estate demo and the AI persona unreachable for detailing leads in every flag combination, campaign-1 messages return False after read-only lookups, its own flag keeps it OFF until the owner switches it, no schema change, easy rollback (DETAILING OFF / STOP ALL / restore 2 files). A prototype already passes 92 new tests, 27 of 27 mutants and the whole backend suite (507 on a patched scratch copy) and its before/after probe shows the intended behaviour.

alternatives_considered.option: A3. Human-only with drafts (no code; what happens today)
alternatives_considered.verdict: KEEP as the interim fallback and as the permanent path for every free-text message, but NOT sufficient alone
alternatives_considered.why: Today a tap lands as a feed row, heartbeat_check wakes the operator lane (heartbeat_check.py:117-123), the closer drafts, the owner replies OK <CODE> and the desktop operator runs wa.py reply (stage 1 needs a code, wa.py:548-556). That is safe but takes minutes to hours and a lead who followed the video's CTA ('write haan') gets silence. It also leaves the leak open: with the AI agent ON a detailing lead gets the real-estate persona, and typing 'send demo' starts the real-estate demo (probe). So at minimum the claim hook is needed; the instant text is the cheap part on top.

alternatives_considered.option: A4. Let the AI sales agent answer with a new detailing knowledge base
alternatives_considered.verdict: REJECT for v1 (revisit after Gate 1 if replies justify it)
alternatives_considered.why: sales_agent.py loads exactly one KB file (KB_PATH, sales_agent.py:96, 216-230) and hard-codes a real-estate persona in SYSTEM_PROMPT (627-648) and tools that promise a free personalised demo (631, 471-475), which contradicts the detailing rules (no free, no price, no guarantee). Swapping the KB would change what campaign-1 leads receive; choosing KB, prompt and tools per template means rewriting a 1,475-line module and its 100+ tests, writing and getting owner approval for a new KB (12 of the 55 current entries are still pending_owner), OpenAI cost and hallucination risk, and free-text replies to cold small-business owners about price and offer are exactly what the first-client rules keep with a human.

alternatives_considered.option: A5. Meta/BSP-side automation (welcome message, ice breakers, away message on the WhatsApp number)
alternatives_considered.verdict: REJECT (unverified that the BSP exposes it)
alternatives_considered.why: It applies to the whole WABA number, so campaign 1 would be affected, it cannot tell which template was tapped, cannot hand off or suppress, and nothing in the repo shows waba.fortius.in.net supports it.

alternatives_considered.option: A6. Answer the yes tap with an interactive mini-flow (buttons and questions like the demo)
alternatives_considered.why: More branches, session state, caps and copy to approve; the detailing offer has nothing to qualify yet (price and sample are the owner's decision), and it would recreate the real-estate demo's complexity inside a first-client test. One fixed acknowledgement plus a human is the smallest safe step; buttons in the reply can be added later as a config entry once the owner knows what to ask.
